setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Jerry badly botched the opening Half-Step and seemed drowsy until later in the set; Reviewer enjoyed the unfamiliar phrasing in the Half-Step [8][9][13]
- **Big River** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds Big River pretty sweet; Reviewer praises Big River and Beat It On Down The Line as strong for typical first-set songs [9][13]
- **It's All Over Now** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it the best It's All Over Now they have heard; Reviewer dislikes Keith grinding chords off Phil here, wanting more runs as he plays in Brown Eyed Women [13][15]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer was annoyed by the information about this song, implying the recording of it is incomplete [7]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Jerry's laryngitis-affected voice gives August West extra gravitas in this song [15]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Lazy Lightning into Supplication is called really good, after which the first set closes [8]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer loves the Phil and drums segment, with the following Space also quite good [11]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer feels Jerry's imperfect singing makes Wharf Rat even better [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-01-13.135501.sbd.miller.flac24** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd78-01-13.sbd.clugston.4629.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 3.53/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the soundboard sounds great; Reviewer says the sound is great [6][15]
- **gd1978-01-13.fob.akgd224e.holwein.menke.motb-0111.105208.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 159 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is decent, but has cracking sounds when the music gets loud [11]
- **gd1978-01-13.135500.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Jerry was still recovering from laryngitis, yet the reviewer thinks that seemed to spark his playing [6]
- The concert was a Pacific Alliance benefit with a Stop Nuclear Power theme [1]
- Second set is judged weaker than the preceding two weeks of shows, falling short of greatness [8]
- Jerry's laryngitis is faintly audible, far less than at Fresno two nights later [11]
- Reviewer finds the pace slow and recommends the Shrine shows for stronger January performances [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-01-13.135501.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> AIFF (24bit/88.2k) [1]. Also: Source is an AKG D224E microphone recording to a cassette master; Brown Eyed Women and Sugar Magnolia gaps are filled with segments from another source, shnid 105208 [1]
- **gd78-01-13.sbd.clugston.4629.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1978-01-13.fob.akgd224e.holwein.menke.motb-0111.105208.flac16**: taped by Reinhart Holwein; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: 2 x AKG D224E >> Sony TC-158SD >> MAC; Analog Audience Source: FOB Master Cassettes (MAC) Medium Stock Brands: MAC = 2 x Maxell UDXL-II Analog [4]
- **gd1978-01-13.135500.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> AIFF (24bit/88.2k) [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Poster - Arlington Theater](https://www.dead.net/archives/1978/artwork/poster-arlington-theater) [18]
